registry_disposition.reason: DSI (dynamic skill selection) adds a new canonical contract to core/contracts/ (skill-selection.schema.json), which is a CONTRACT_RECORD class change under the registry-disposition.v1 consumer binding and under this repo's adopted relevance classes (CONTRACT_RECORD, PROVENANCE, SUPERSESSION). The Unitera registry must gain a representation of the new contract surface and of the deterministic skill-selection decision it records. The registry write is its own registered change and follows after the owner merges the source change (precedent: the S4 slice in pull request 50, which followed the same two-phase REQUIRED_BUT_BLOCKED -> UPDATED rebind pattern). This slice does not perform the registry write, so no registry commit exists yet and registry_commit_sha stays null; implementation_commit_sha is bound by the follow-up rebind commit of this branch and is the commit that carries the implementation. The determination is stated explicitly rather than left implicit: this change IS registry relevant, and affected_records therefore is NOT empty. The change set was rebased onto origin/main (27b17b62800d5d37e14bfe48ecd210603c4e1cb6) and then onto the current origin/main (bfa56ec17306ab709be3d492f02ac27150b4661a, which carries the S8 governance-promotion slice, the S4 skill-improvement-analyzer slice and the SII rebind) so that the branch carries the DSI slice alone and no S4 change - S4 is now part of the base and of no other slice's diff; the rebinds do not alter the set of affected records, which is still exactly one new canonical contract.
